card.title: Still Part of This
card.instruction: Act as though shared history permanently guarantees your place, even when present boundaries suggest otherwise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've hung my coat on my old hook. What's for dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You moved out three years ago.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We use that space for guests now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the guests their hook has an owner.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 resumes the old coat hook and dinner expectation, A3 treats the surviving hook as a surviving place, and A5 asserts ownership despite the guest boundary.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's moved-out reminder causes A3's object-continuity answer; B4's guest use causes A5's competing owner claim.

relationship.evidence: B2 establishes the current boundary and B4 explains the household's present use of the space.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's guests as recipients of A's old-place claim, though the demand develops only slightly.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 clearly establish a former resident acting as if still at home.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's the-hook-did-not answer and A5's owner claim are compact expressions of historical entitlement.
